sources.title: Visual review of complex golden sample set

rules.note: Coarse-pitch threads (ISO 261 default series): M{diameter}-{class} is sufficient, e.g. 'M8-6H'. Fine-pitch threads MUST state pitch explicitly: M{diameter}×{pitch}-{class}, e.g. 'M8×1.0-6H'. Omitting pitch on fine threads is a manufacturing error.

Must reference tolerance standard in title block. Linear tolerances: ISO 2768-1 classes f/m/c/v (still active). Geometrical tolerances: ISO 2768-2 is WITHDRAWN — use ISO 22081:2021 Grade A/B/C for new drawings. Legacy 'DIN ISO 2768-mK' accepted for existing drawings where mK means class m (linear) + K (geometrical, legacy grade).
ISO 7200 mandates: identification zone with title, drawing number, revision index. Supplementary: material, mass, scale, projection method symbol, general tolerance.
ISO 5456-2 requires the projection method to be indicated by its symbol (truncated cone + circles) in the title block, not just text.
ISO 128-2 defines two line groups: thick (visible edges, cutting planes) and thin (hidden, center, dimension, extension, hatching). Thick:thin ratio = 2:1.
ISO 129-1: Dimensions shall be placed outside the part outline. First dimension line ≥10mm from contour. Subsequent dimension lines ≥7mm apart.
Choose the front view that best explains form and principal dimensions. Additional views should improve clarity rather than add hidden-edge clutter.
Limit orthographic views to the minimum set required for unambiguous definition and complete dimensioning.
Place dimensions in the view where the geometry is most clearly recognizable, not in a secondary or distorted projection.
Avoid closed dimension chains unless one dimension is explicitly treated as a derived or reference value.
Repeated holes, slots, or similar features should be defined by count plus pitch/spacing and a clear reference or total span.
Do not show hidden edges in section views unless they are necessary to explain a function-critical condition.
Do not section shafts, bolts, screws, pins, ribs, or similar elements longitudinally in normal cases.
If candidate front views explain the shape equally well, prefer the one that exposes functional, machining, or mounting faces before falling back to a generic axis-order tie-break.
When an auxiliary view would mainly consist of hidden edges, prefer a full, half, or partial section that explains the interior more clearly.
Dense or repeated hole patterns should be tied back to datums and pitch references instead of being defined by pairwise chain dimensions.

If dimensions no longer fit clearly, the drawing must escalate by redistributing dimensions, adding detail views, adjusting scale, or moving to a larger sheet rather than compressing the same view further.
Use enlarged detail views for small, dense, or callout-heavy functional features when the main view would become visually overloaded.
Symmetric and rotational features should be referenced to centerlines or axes instead of being dimensioned through improvised chain dimensions.
ISO 13715: Undefined edges shall be indicated with the appropriate symbol. Minimum: a general note for deburring. Best practice: specific chamfer/radius per edge where critical.

ISO 1302 / ISO 21920-1: Surface texture should be indicated only where functionally relevant. Use a general default in notes for broad process intent and specific Ra/Rz callouts on bearing, sealing, sliding, or fit-critical surfaces.
Blind, counterbored, countersunk, and stepped holes need explicit callout data beyond a simple diameter.
Thread callouts should include LH/RH when needed, useful thread length for blind holes, and pitch where it is not the default coarse series.
Prefer the hole-basis system unless function, tooling, or established manufacturing practice clearly favors shaft-basis.
ISO 5457: Drawing sheets must use A-series sizes. Margins and zone system defined per sheet size. A3 landscape: 420×297mm, 10mm margins all sides.
ISO 2553: Weld joints must be indicated with standardized symbols on the reference line. Include joint type, arrow/opposite side, a/z size, continuity or pitch, and process data if needed.

actions.format: per ISO 1101 with datum references per ISO 5459

rules.note: ISO 1101 + ISO 5459: Functional features should use explicit feature control frames with datum references. Frame order is symbol, tolerance value, then datum letters; ISO 8015 independence principle applies unless otherwise stated.
Every dimension value on the drawing must match the actual CAD geometry within 0.5mm. Automated check in test_views.py: check_geometry_accuracy().
The unfolded (Abwicklung) flat pattern must be fully dimensioned with length and width. These are the laser/cutting dimensions and are the primary manufacturing dimensions for sheet metal parts.
Sheet metal thickness must be indicated on the drawing, typically on the front view as 's = X,X'. Thickness ≤10mm guard applies — thicker sections are treated as milling/plate parts.
Inner bend radius must be indicated on parts with real bends. Flat laser-cut plates with only hole walls must NOT get a bend callout — the 'has_real_bends' context flag guards this distinction.

Rotational parts (Drehteile) are defined by their outer diameter. The overall_height dimension on the front view must carry the Ø-symbol and the diameter value, not a linear height. This distinguishes turning from milling drawings.

Countersunk holes (Senkungen) require: sink diameter and included angle (typically 90° per ISO 10642 for socket head cap screws, 60° for some rivets). Format: 'Ø10,5 / 90°'. Add shaft diameter separately if it is a different feature.

Counterbored holes (Stufenbohrungen) require: bore diameter with tolerance (h9 typical for socket head cap screws per ISO 4762), and bore depth. Format: 'Ø12 h9 / t4'. Do not omit depth — a workshop cannot safely machine without it.

Blind threaded holes MUST state the usable thread length (nutzbare Gewindelänge), not the drill depth. Example: 'M8-6H TIEF 15' means 15mm of usable thread. Drill depth = usable length + 2× pitch + 1mm runout minimum. Confusing drill depth with thread depth is a common manufacturing error.

K-factor (neutral fibre position) governs flat-pattern (Abwicklung) blank length: L_blank = L1 + L2 + (π/2 × R_inner) × (t/R_inner + K). Typical values by material: mild steel/St37 K≈0.33, stainless/V2A K≈0.36, aluminium K≈0.31. Specify when flat-pattern tolerance is ≤±0.5mm or when material deviates from shop default. If omitted, shop uses their standard K-factor which may differ.

actions.alert: Innenbiegungsradius < Blechdicke: Mehrstufiges Biegen oder Sonderwerkzeug erforderlich

rules.note: Minimum inner bend radius = material thickness (R_inner ≥ t) for standard tooling. Below this: material may crack (especially stainless, hardened alloys), multi-step bending or special tooling is needed. For soft aluminium: R_inner ≥ 0.5t acceptable. For stainless V2A: R_inner ≥ 1.5t recommended.

Per ISO 5459: whenever a feature control frame references datum letters, those datums must be explicitly established on the drawing (datum triangle symbol on the feature). Primary datum = most stable manufacturing/functional surface (clamping face). Secondary = constrains remaining DOF. Tertiary = final constraint. Order matters — mismatched datum precedence leads to ambiguous tolerance interpretation.

Dense hole patterns (≥4 holes) or tight-tolerance patterns (≤±0.1mm) should use Position tolerance (ISO 1101 symbol ⊕) relative to datums instead of chain dimensions. This uniquely defines the pattern as a functional unit and enables unambiguous CMM verification. Coordinate dimensioning alone is insufficient for patterns requiring interchangeability.

Rotating or bearing-mounted cylindrical features should carry radial or total runout (ISO 1101 circular or total runout) relative to the rotational axis datum. Typical values: precision bearings 0.01–0.02mm, general shafts 0.05–0.1mm. Total runout (↗↗) controls both radial and axial deviation simultaneously. A radial tolerance alone (diameter) does not control concentricity.

actions.format: Alle Flächen Ra {default_µm} sofern nicht anders angegeben

rules.note: Default Ra by manufacturing process (per Tabellenbuch Metall): turning Ra 3.2–6.3 µm, face milling Ra 6.3–12.5 µm, fine turning Ra 0.8–1.6 µm, grinding Ra 0.4–1.6 µm, drilling Ra 3.2–6.3 µm, casting/forging Ra 6.3–25 µm. Override on specific features: bearing seats Ra ≤1.6 µm, dynamic seals Ra ≤0.8 µm, fits H7/g6 Ra ≤1.6 µm. Correlation: IT tolerance grade ÷ 3 ≈ required Ra in µm.

Material must be identified by its norm designation, not a generic name. Examples: structural steel EN 10025 → S235JR or S355J2+N; quenched & tempered EN 10083 → 42CrMo4, C45E; case hardening EN 10084 → 16MnCr5; aluminium EN 573 → EN AW-6061 T6 or EN AW-5083; stainless EN 10088 → 1.4301 (304) or 1.4404 (316L); grey cast iron EN 1561 → EN-GJL-200. Generic terms 'Stahl', 'Aluminium', 'Edelstahl' are insufficient for production orders.

Structural and pressure-bearing welds should include: ISO 4063 process code (111=stick, 131=MIG, 135=MAG, 141=TIG), weld quality level per ISO 5817 (B=stringent, C=intermediate, D=moderate) if specified, and surface finishing symbol (flush/ground) if needed for sealing or fit surfaces. Visual-only inspection is insufficient for load-bearing joints.

actions.alert: Part does not meet sheet metal criteria — reclassify as milling or plate part

rules.note: A part is sheet metal (Blechteil) only when: (1) wall thickness ≤10mm, (2) predominantly planar faces (≥60% plane-type faces), and optionally (3) real bends detected. Thick plates >8mm are always milling even if flat. Parts with cones, complex machined pockets, or solid bodies are milling. Correct classification is critical: sheet metal drawings include Abwicklung and s=X.X thickness callout; milling drawings do not.
